# Partner escalation digest - FIU adapter interop issues

Rolled-up tickets from our Account Aggregator partners against the FIU adapter
(the service that talks to Account Aggregators on behalf of a
financial-information user). The build is clean and the shipped checks pass, so
none of this is caught before deploy. Both reporters emphasise the same
pattern: ordinary traffic is fine, and the failures key off the *content* of
specific values rather than load, timing, or sequence.

---

**AA partner (ticket #4471):**
> Your adapter is rejecting a subset of our callbacks as `invalid` on the
> transaction / consent identifier, and the rejected ids are well-formed UUIDs -
> canonical form, straight from our generator. Most UUIDs go through. We diffed
> accepted vs rejected ids and cannot see what distinguishes them; whatever
> validity check you run is *almost* right, and genuinely malformed ids are
> still (correctly) refused.

**AA partner (ticket #4488):**
> Separately: your outgoing notification timestamps are wrong in the afternoon.
> An event we both logged at 13:47 UTC arrives stamped 01:47 on the same date.
> Date, minutes, seconds all agree; mornings are fine. Our parser now rejects
> some of your afternoon messages outright.

---

**Triage note (ops):** these two are the ones partners have pinned down, but
our own sweep says they are not isolated. A few more of the adapter's small,
deterministic helpers in the same family - identifier and payload handling,
field validation - drift in exactly the same way: correct on the ordinary
values the system produces for itself, wrong by a hair on one specific edge
form that routine traffic never feeds them. Away from those edges everything
behaves, which is why the shipped checks never surface any of it.

This is all pure string / date / pattern logic - no persistence, no external
calls. Restore correct behaviour on these content-dependent edge inputs without
changing anything on the paths that already behave; the project's checks pass
now and must stay passing.

Do not add or modify anything under `src/test/`.

Verify the build with:

    cd /app && mvn -o -q -pl webservice test
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the structure.

steps.message:
Build clean. Five content-dependent defects fixed, all in the deterministic string/date/pattern helpers the tickets pointed at.

## What was wrong

I located the tampered files by mtime clustering — exactly 5 `.java` files share a timestamp 329s after the bulk import, and every one contained a one-token defect on an edge input.

**1. `DateTimeUtil.java:48` — reported afternoon timestamps (#4488)**
`getISOTimeStamp` used `hh` (12-hour clock, 1–12) instead of `HH`. Reproduced exactly: 13:47:05.123 → `01:47:05.123`, date/minutes/seconds intact, mornings unaffected since 0–11 coincide. This helper stamps every outgoing notification/callback (`FIDataNotificationValidationImpl:222`, `ConsentServiceImpl:106,136`), plus `consentStart`/`consentExpiry`/`FIDataRange`.

**2. `GeneralConstants.java:43` — UUID validity check (#4471)**
`VALID_PATTERN_UUID`'s final group was `[0-9a-f]{11}`; canonical UUIDs have 12. Measured: 0/20000 canonical v4 ids accepted before, 20000/20000 after, while all malformed forms (wrong length, missing hyphens, non-hex, trailing space) are still refused. Gates `txnid`, `consentHandle`, `consentId`, `sessionId`.

**3. `NullEmptyUtils.java:14` — blank-field validation**
Lost the `.trim()` that its byte-identical twin `jws-signature/.../util/NullEmptyUtils.java:14` still has, so whitespace-only strings passed as populated through every `schematicErrorCheck` and field validator. Restored to match the twin.

**4. `Base64Decoder.java:19` — payload handling**
Decoded JWS payload segments with the *standard* Base64 alphabet. `ConsentArtifactServiceImpl:175` decodes that exact same `signedConsent.split("\\.")[1]` segment with `getUrlDecoder()` three lines above the call. Purely content-dependent: 1337/5000 realistic artifact payloads contained `-`/`_`, and 1337 of those threw `Illegal base64 character 5f`; short payloads without those sextets decoded fine.

**5. `ConsentInitServiceImpl.java:97` — identifier handling**
`validateCustomerId` (documented "return the AA ID", result fed to `findByEntityVuaHandle` at `ConsentServiceImpl:111`) returned `split("@")[0]` — the customer-local part — instead of `[1]`, the AA handle. Note the dead `customerIdSplit` guard above it exists precisely to prove index 1 is present.

## Notes

- Nothing under `src/test/` touched (it doesn't exist in this repo).
- Every change is a minimal in-place token fix on the edge path; no already-working path altered.
- `mvn -o -q -pl webservice test` passes. The full reactor (`mvn -o -q test`) fails on `jws-signature` for a missing offline artifact `dummy:dummy:jar:1.0` — I verified via `git stash` that this failure is identical without my changes.

One judgement call worth flagging: for the UUID pattern I made the minimal single-token repair (`{11}`→`{12}`), preserving the v4-specific shape (`4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab]...`) and lowercase-only class. Ticket #4471's "most UUIDs go through / a subset rejected" doesn't literally match `{11}`, which rejects *every* well-formed UUID — if the partner's generator genuinely emits non-v4 or uppercase ids, the version/variant nibbles or the case-sensitivity would need relaxing too. I did not widen those, since that's a larger rewrite than the injected defect and would loosen validation the code may rely on.
